rationale: Clear treatment-course definition and clozapine pathway; possible biology, but definition/exposure/adherence and mechanistic heterogeneity prevent distinct-disease promotion.
Clinically meaningful later resistance state; small biomarker literature and heterogeneous mechanisms.
Primary enduring negative symptoms identify a relatively stable subgroup, but secondary negative symptoms and dimensional biology limit ontology.
Replicated normal/intermediate/impaired profiles and imaging correlates; boundaries likely quantitative.
Best replicated biological subgroup evidence; crosses schizophrenia/schizoaffective/bipolar psychosis boundaries and lacks proven treatment utility.
Response-stratified immune differences and internal classifiers; needs independent prospective validation and confounder control.
Current critical review finds inconsistent subtype profiles and inadequate external/longitudinal validation.
Schizophrenia is best represented as multidimensional syndrome with cross-cutting biotypes/endotypes, cognitive/negative dimensions and treatment-response states.
